Subject: POC: message format, auth & streaming behavior (post-demo)

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good signal on the integration fit. I captured a short recap and the engineering questions we promised to send so your team can validate feasibility before the tech-deep-dive. Please confirm or correct any details below.

Recap (agreed/high-level)
- Redwood will provide a short SDK quickstart and example payloads for the POC (Python + Node).
- Auth model: service-account style API keys / JWT for server authors; short-lived tokens preferred.
- Routing: we need per-request region hints + fallback policy (latency -> cost).
- Structured output/tool calling: support for function/tool schema with deterministic sniffing + size limits.
- Embeddings & reranker: store embeddings in your vector DB; Redwood to return reranker scores and a confidence threshold.
- Message format decisions: chat vs completions model choice, token budgeting, stop sequences, streaming semantics.

Engineering questions (please reply inline where possible)
1) SDK + quickstart
   - Which SDK versions do you want us to provide? Any internal code style constraints?
   - Example payloads: do you need both chat-format and completions-format examples?

2) Auth
   - Preferred token lifecycle (rotate every X hours)? Support for signed JWTs or OAuth client credentials?
   - Any IP allowlists / mTLS requirements for the POC?

3) Routing / regional hints
   - We can accept an x-redwood-region header and a priority hint. Do you have a single region preference or need geo-fallback?

4) Structured tool calling
   - Will the tool outputs be stored server-side (for retrieval) or streamed back to the client only? Any hard limits for tool result size?

5) Embeddings / reranker
   - Embedding dim you use and similarity threshold for the reranker? Will you re-rank top-K or score pairwise on candidate sets?

6) Request/response schema specifics
   - Chat vs completions: any constraints that force one over the other?
   - Tokenization: do you have an internal token-counting approach (tiktoken/etc)? Expected max sequence lengths?
   - Stop sequences: any custom stop tokens required for returning structured payloads?
   - Streaming: do you expect interim partial tokens, or prefer chunked “sentence” events + final complete object?

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (POC milestones)

Next steps
- Please reply with engineering answers inline. If everything matches, we’ll schedule the tech deep-dive (45m) focused on SDK auth & message contracts.

Thanks —

Thanks, Soojin — great write-up. I answered inline below and added a few pragmatic constraints to keep the POC lean.

1) SDK + quickstart- We’d like Python and Node examples (our backend services are Python). Target SDK versions: redwood-python >=0.9.0 and redwood-node >=0.8.0.
- Example payloads: yes, both chat and completions examples would be helpful. Also include an example showing a streaming chat call that ends with a structured tool invocation.

2) Auth- We prefer service-account JWTs minted by our internal auth service; tokens rotate every 12–24 hours. OAuth client-credentials are OK as an alternative. No mTLS for the POC; IP allowlist is fine later for prod.

3) Routing / regional hints- Use x-redwood-region with values (us-west-2 | us-east-1 | eu-west-1). Also honor x-redwood-priority with values (low|normal|high) for fallback choices. Primary region for POC: us-west-2 with us-east-1 as latency fallback.

4) Structured tool calling- Tool outputs will be streamed back to client by default. For the POC we’ll keep tool payloads < 32KB. If Redwood will accept and persist tool outputs, great — otherwise plan for client storage. Include a size-limit error code in the spec.

5) Embeddings / reranker- We use 1536-d embeddings (Open-embedding compat). Rerank is top-K re-scoring (K=50) with pairwise scoring and then thresholding — please surface both raw scores and a normalized confidence in the response. Target reranker pass-through threshold ~0.7.

6) Request/response schema specifics
- Chat vs completions: multi-turn flows => chat (preserve role/turn metadata). Single-turn classification/generation => completions. For the POC we’ll default chat for session flows.
- Tokenization: we use tiktoken (cl100k_base). Expect 8k token model budget; we’ll handle client-side truncation for histories but want server-side truncated flag and approximate token counts returned.
- Max tokens: cap per-request 4096 for completions-style calls and 8192 for dedicated chat flows at POC. Please include a response header like x-redwood-tokens-used.
- Stop sequences: we will use JSON-encapsulated stop tokens for structured outputs (e.g., "
--END-JSON--"). Server should close stream immediately when a stop is seen and emit a final completion event.
- Streaming semantics: we expect per-token streaming with an explicit finalization message. For structured outputs prefer chunked JSON events rather than token-by-token reassembly — an approach that emits valid JSON chunks reduces client parsing risk. Provide a streaming=true header to opt-in.

Attachments: I uploaded a short quickstart (redwood_sdk_quickstart.md) and a small example_payloads.json to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-poc

If that all looks good we’re ready for the tech deep-dive. I can bring one of our infra engineers to discuss routing and tokenization edge cases.

—Alex
